title: Mucktracker
summary: Redesigned a media-literacy platform for high school classrooms in five weeks. Afterwards, 75% of students surveyed said it felt designed for them.
tagline: A media-literacy platform, redesigned in five weeks. 75% of surveyed students said it felt designed for them.
intro: Mucktracker helps high school students build media literacy by working with live news from trusted sources. The platform worked, but it lacked structure and visual consistency. As Lead Product Designer, I worked daily with the founder and the engineering lead to redesign the core student and teacher experiences and build the product’s first design system, all in a five-week sprint.
body:
## Key objectives

- Make the student and teacher experiences clearer and more engaging, within the limits of an existing, developer-built platform.
- Deliver a clickable prototype for the team’s National Science Foundation pitch.
- Lay a design foundation so the product stays consistent as it grows.

## Where it started

In early testing, students didn’t feel Mucktracker was made for them. They called it visually boring and “not for my grade,” though they could see it would help with class and research. Making it feel like theirs became the brief.

## Process

I started with a fast audit and research round: personas, a competitive analysis and flow mapping. From there I prototyped in Figma and checked feasibility with the engineer every day. Each prototype went straight to the CLIPsters, a panel of volunteer teachers and students from [Character Lab](https://characterlab.org/), who tried it and gave us feedback right away.

![Design process timeline](/images/mucktracker/emily-lange-portfolio-march-2025.png)

*The five-week design process.*

![Mucktracker personas](/images/mucktracker/mucktracker-personas.png)

*Personas for students and teachers.*

![Mucktracker competitor audit](/images/mucktracker/mucktracker-competitor-audit.png)

*Competitive analysis.*

## Simplifying navigation

Students had too many places to go and no clear path between them. I simplified the information architecture and unified navigation across the student and teacher views.

![Learner information architecture before and after](/images/mucktracker/emily-lange-portfolio-march-2025-3.png)

*The student flow before and after.*

## Redesigning the core tools

I focused on the screens students use most: Home, Assignments, and the two research tools, Canvas and Timeline, where students collect, organize and analyze news.

On **Canvas**, I moved the side navigation to the top, made the article cards more visual, and added toggles to switch views, organizer tools and a dotted grid to arrange work on.

![Canvas view before](/images/mucktracker/emily-lange-portfolio-march-2025-4.png)

*Canvas, before.*

![Canvas view after](/images/mucktracker/emily-lange-portfolio-march-2025-5.png)

*Canvas, after.*

Students loved the list and timeline toggle on **Timeline**, but asked to see their current assignment and to interact with their teacher. I added the assignment to the view, annotations and sticky notes, and easier navigation through time.

![Timeline view before](/images/mucktracker/emily-lange-portfolio-march-2025-6.png)

*Timeline, before.*

![Timeline view after](/images/mucktracker/emily-lange-portfolio-march-2025-8.png)

*Timeline, after.*

The article card appears in search, the timeline and every news feed, so I redesigned it to be something teenagers actually want to open: emoji reactions for engagement, and hierarchy built with color instead of shadows.

![Article cards before and after](/images/mucktracker/mucktracker-s-article-cards.png)

*The original article card (left) and my redesign (right).*

I also designed new features, suggested topics and a student profile, and a multi-step assignment flow for teachers building lessons and managing a class.

## A design foundation

I built Mucktracker’s first design library: typography, a color palette and reusable components, so the engineer could build new features consistently.

![Design system foundation](/images/mucktracker/emily-lange-portfolio-march-2025-12.png)

*The design system foundation.*

## Outcome

In a CLIPster survey after the redesign, **75% of students said the app felt designed for them**. In their words: “Very easy for high schoolers to use” and “Has a great vibe.”

The redesign also became the prototype for the team’s National Science Foundation pitch in the VITAL competition, where Mucktracker reached the semifinals. Beyond the screens, I helped set product priorities, balancing feedback, scope and speed.
